newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures rally,end near highs.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures rally,end near highs.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures rallied again in late trading to end sharply higher and hugging day's highs.
Traders said the ability of the Dow 30 Industrials to close above the 5,900 level for the first time persuaded more shorts to even up and new longs to enter.
"I think it was some short-covering from guys who got short and some guys who got long heading into tomorrow," said one floor broker in Standard & Poor's 500 futures.
A strong performance in U.S. Treasury bond futures, which widened their gains late, kept stock index futures supported.

T-bond futures, which rose during the morning on soft economic data, gained more ground late on ideas that Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan does not view current U.S. inflation as a risk and that U.S. rates will not rise.

The Australian Financial Review reported in its Wednesday edition that Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, who met with Greenspan in Washington, said the Fed chairman was "very optimistic" about inflation.
Some traders also noted signs of computerized buy programs in the cash market on the advance, which widened the premium enough to trigger index arbitrage buy programs as well.

"We had a flurry of buy programs on the way up. It looked like we had some cash-only programs and some index arb," said a floor analyst in S&P 500s. "It looked fund buying in the cash market. There wasn't a whole lot over here. The locals had been trying to play the short side."

Fair value on Tuesday, based on the London Interbank Offered Rate, was about 5.40 points premium. Arbitrage buy programs needed about 6.10 points over cash. Sell programs required about 4.75 points premium.
The final leg up in December S&P 500s left them at a 5.92-point premium over cash.
A weaker than expected September national purchasing managers index, which dipped to 51.7 from August's 52.6, helped hoist T-bond futures and S&P 500s upward early before the rise flagged.
Stock futures eroded near midday but then began rebounding as over-the-counter stocks showed signs of recouping some of their losses.

At settlement, Dec S&P 500s were up 3.70 to 695.10, Value Lines gained 1.70 pts to 643.70, Nikkei lost 70.0 to 21,505.0, Midcap eased 0.05 to 243.90, and NYSE Composite advanced 2.40 to 371.30. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
